implement.approach: Started from exactly BASE_SHA 608bf7b4; cherry-picked the three sound r4 commits (cc2eb199 tests, 2f4072a2 feature, 624d2b55 fix) so the admission module, the two production-path gates and the r4 regression suite are reused verbatim. Round-5 regression tests were written first, shown to fail (8 failures) on the r4 code, and committed separately (0ef869fd). Root cause in importAdmission.ts candidatesFor(): `preparation` (a peak >= 2.5x louder within 700 ms after this one) was computed first and `comparable = !preparation && (absoluteFloor || ratioToStrongest)`, so the demotion overrode the absolute 4 torso-lengths/s stroke floor. Fix (b391819a): comparability is decided per candidate on its own evidence only — `comparable = peakTorsoPerSecond >= minStrokePeakTorsoPerSecond || peakSpeed >= strongest * comparablePeakRatio`; `preparationWindowMs` is removed from IMPORT_ADMISSION_LIMITS (it is provably dead once the floor has precedence: any candidate >= 0.4x the strongest peak is >= 0.4x every later peak, so `preparation` could only ever be true for candidates the ratio test already excluded). Both remaining tests can only ADD comparable events as motion is added, so comparableEventCount is monotonic and a harder appended stroke can never demote a real one; a genuine sub-stroke wind-up (below the floor AND below 0.4x the strongest) is still excluded by those two tests alone, which is what the 'sub-stroke wind-up ... ONE stroke' test pins. No hard-coding of the adversarial examples; no change to the two shipping gates in runCaptureAnalysis.ts beyond the r4 wiring (the ambiguous rally now fails the existing pre-permit gate on both the session-less and saved-original paths, which the two new end-to-end tests prove).

This is deliberate, not an omission: the native import payload (ClipMediaStore.swift buildClipPayload) exports only uri/durationMs/width/height/fps/byteSize/nativeMediaIdentity — no rotation, codec or track count reaches JS — and fabricating those values is prohibited. Exporting them requires apps/mobile/src/camera/capture.ts (outside write_paths) and apps/mobile/ios/LocalPods/ (serial group native-pod, not held by this package). INFERRED from Swift source: the native preflight already rejects >1 video track, non-finite preferredTransform, over-limit dimensions/fps before a clip exists, so the JS gate is defence in depth for facts JS cannot currently measure. residual_risks: Two volleys whose peaks fall within sameEventPeakDistanceMs (350 ms) of each other with a valley above 50 % of the lesser peak are still one event (the contact-dip allowance); a third such volley within any 350 ms window is refused, and a dead stop between two 340 ms-apart strokes is refused. Realistic fast hand battles (≥ 3 exchanges or a stop) are covered; a lone two-contact 300 ms double-tap that never slows below half speed is not.

A backward movement immediately after a stroke that is slower than half the stroke's peak and continuous with it is folded as the recovery — a very soft backhand right after a hard drive (≤ 50 % of its speed, opposite travel) is indistinguishable from a recovery by wrist speed alone. A stroke-sized burst relative to its neighbour (> 50 %) is always a second stroke; an absolute floor was tried and rejected because a hard drive's own backswing legitimately exceeds 4 torso/s.

Synthetic swings with per-frame landmark noise ≥ ~2 % of image height are refused as multiple events (prominence 1.5 torso/s); ≤ 1 % noise is admitted. Real Vision jitter on a stable phone is well below 1 %; a heavily shaking capture will be refused rather than mis-admitted (conservative direction).
implement.summary: W03-01 round 6 resolves all three adversary breaks on top of the sound r5 work (cherry-picked 24ccabb9..3011ac87 onto BASE 608bf7b4, then be7d5c0b tests → 8893f612 fix; 04a09361/2dd70342 add and retract one test, 42bf4c60 removes its rule — see below). Defects scoped on the r5 candidate b391819a in apps/mobile/src/camera/importAdmission.ts: (1) `distinctPeakRatio` compared every peak of a wrist with that wrist's MEDIAN speed, so a constant paddle-hand speed offset raised the median until every stroke of a rally fell below the ratio and the wrist vanished, leaving the lone off-hand gesture as THE stroke (non-monotonic admission); (2) `comparablePeakRatio` judged comparability as a share of the LOUDEST event, so adding a harder burst demoted real strokes; (3) `groupPeaks` fused any two peaks whose valley stayed above `eventValleyRatio` (0.5) regardless of spacing, so four volleys every 450 ms with 60 % valleys became one < 2 s 'stroke'. Fix (all inside write_paths): comparability is now an absolute body-normalised floor per event (`minComparablePeakTorsoPerSecond: 2`) — no whole-wrist or loudest-relative ratio remains (pinned by the 'publishes absolute floors only' test); `groupPeaks` fuses peaks only across a contact dip (second peak ≤ `sameEventPeakDistanceMs` 350 ms from the event's FIRST peak with valley > 50 % of the lesser peak) or when the dip is jitter (< `minPeakProminenceTorsoPerSecond` 1.5 torso/s below the lesser peak, measured against the event's highest peak so a jitter plateau cannot chain separate strokes), and never across a tracking gap; `clusterComparable` admits at most one event per wrist per cluster (both wrists of one swing still merge; two same-wrist events 340 ms apart are two strokes); wind-up/recovery folding is direction-aware (`isStrokePhase`: ≤ `maxWindUpPeakRatio` 0.5 of the stroke, continuous within `maxWindUpPauseMs` 400, no gap, net travel ≥ `minDirectedTravelTorso` 0.2 for both, direction cosine ≤ `maxWindUpDirectionCosine` −0.3), with each fold recorded in `phaseOf` and at most one phase per side; an over-long motion span is judged `motion_not_stroke_like` before clip-edge truncation. Shipping wiring unchanged from r5 and re-verified: `runCaptureAnalysis()` (session-less) and `runOriginalCaptureAnalysis()` (saved-original) both call `admitImportedClip` before `POST /v1/analysis-permits`, before inference and before the durable attempt row — the 6 new 'round 6:' shipping-path tests assert fetch is never called, no reservation, no inference, no attempt. During r6 I tried an additional absolute rule (a wind-up/recovery must also peak below the 4 torso/s stroke floor) with a regression test (04a09361 + 8893f612); the pre-existing r5 suites 'is monotonic: a much stronger third stroke…', 'keeps dink, dink, drive a rally' and 'appending ANY admitted stroke…' proved a hard drive's own backswing exceeds that floor (3 failures), so the rule and its test were withdrawn in follow-up commits 2dd70342 (test) and 42bf4c60 (impl) rather than by rewriting history; no pre-existing test was weakened, skipped, deleted or reordered.
